provisional: Written by hand on 2026-11-20, before the findings log exists (same form as 196.json). Fields follow the finding format in issue #198 (02); issue #200 (03b) defines the log's file format and takes this file over. All are Low, so none failed #197 (the human's ruling: QA fails only on Medium or Critical) and none gets its own issue.

findings.recommendation: Hold `Ruling:` to the same spacing rule as `Overrides:` and `Waiver:`.
findings.what: `Ruling:X=v` (no space after the colon) and extra spaces after the colon are still applied (agent-kit/scripts/settings.py near line 435). Values are fully checked either way.

findings.recommendation: Match the first line exactly (`Orchestrator: Ruling`) and check `Human ruled:` is a real date.
findings.what: Any first line starting `Orchestrator: Ruling` counts as a ruling, e.g. `Orchestrator: Rulings recap` (settings.py near line 420), as C6 literally says. `Human ruled:` accepts impossible dates such as 2026-99-99 (near line 149).

findings.recommendation: #218 must pass the WAIVABLE_GATES value from read_settings; or read_rulings also checks each gate against the setting's own allowed list and refuses a plain string.
findings.what: read_rulings trusts its `waivable` argument: called with ("push",) it accepts `Waiver: push - x`; a plain string is split into single characters (settings.py near line 454). Safe through read_settings today.

findings.recommendation: Catch RecursionError in load_issue and refuse with a `settings:` reason.
findings.what: An extremely deeply nested dump raises an uncaught RecursionError in load_issue (settings.py near line 487) instead of a `settings:` refusal. Still exit 1 with empty stdout; a real gh dump can't produce it.

findings.recommendation: Refuse lines that look like an `Overrides:` line but aren't at column 1 (quote, `1)` list, non-breaking-space indent), as bullets already are.
findings.what: `> Overrides:`, `1) Overrides:` and a line indented with a non-breaking space are silently ignored: neither applied nor refused. Fails safe.

findings.recommendation: Skip null-author and non-owner comments before checking their fields, so a malformed foreign comment can't block the read.
findings.what: A null-author comment missing `body` or `createdAt` is refused rather than skipped (the Engineer's stated choice; fails closed).

findings.recommendation: Treat a present-but-blank N as a usage error, as `make issue-hash N=` does.
findings.what: `make settings N=` or `make settings "N= "` runs without the issue levels and exits 0 (Makefile lines 22-25, agent-kit/templates/Makefile.mk lines 29-32: `$(if $(value N),...)` treats a blank N as no N). A forgotten number at the pre-launch step would miss an issue-level refusal. Matches C3 literally; no bound can be crossed.

One non-owner comment with a malformed field (null body, missing createdAt, author without login) refuses the whole read (settings.py lines 413-419), before the owner filter. Real REST comments can't produce this; fails closed.
A refusal reason reads "a Overrides: line" (settings.py line 333).
